api-key-id.description:
**Unique identifier for API key**

Please use the `api-key-id` provided by Linktivity as-is.

Example: `VJgSBDVXXXXXXXXX`
api-key-id.name: api-key-id

group-id.description:
**Unique identifier for Group belonging to OTA**

Please use the `group-id` provided by Linktivity as-is.

Example: `[default-group]:LINKTIVITY`
group-id.name: group-id

ota-id.description:
**Unique identifier for OTA**

Please use the `ota-id` provided by Linktivity as-is.

Example: `LINKTIVITY`
ota-id.name: ota-id

signature-key.description:
**API signature key**

An HMAC-based signature calculated per request. To calculate the signature, you must have:

  - apiKey - the API key which is created by GDS service and only stored on your own servers.
  - timestamp - the [timestamp](#section/Authentication/timestamp) header field value.
  - host - the API host, e.g. "open-agent.gds-neo.link-dev.link".
  - path - the operation path, e.g. "/v1/search-activities".

For the algorithm and runnable code samples in JavaScript, Go, Python, Java, and PHP, see the **Signature Algorithm** and **Client snippets** subsections under [Authentication](#section/Authentication).

Example: `3gjtSDLmvsr4M6RdQ9vY5sYPZ1Y7iVXXXXXXXXXXXXX=`
signature-key.name: signature-key

timestamp.description:
**Current timestamp**

The timestamp should be in <Day(YYYYMMDD) + "T" + Time(HHMMSS) + "Z"> format, e.g. 20060102T150405Z.

**The timestamp must be within ±5 minutes of the actual API call time.**

Example: `20260521T063324Z`
timestamp.name: timestamp

get.description: Returns the full set in one response (no pagination).

Returns a paginated list of activity overviews. Use the returned
`next_cursor` to fetch the following page.

parameters.name: supplier_ids
parameters.description:
Optional. Limit the search to activities offered by these suppliers.
Example supplier ids: `SKYTREE`, `SAGANO`, `JRWEST`.

parameters.name: activity_ids
parameters.description: Optional. Limit the search to specific activity ids.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Optional. Free-text keyword to match against the activity title. Language-sensitive.

parameters.name: language_code
parameters.description:
Optional. Display language for activity / plan text in the response.
If unset, results are returned in every available language (each text field carries all translations).
Note: the availability endpoints require `language_code` because they return single-language strings.

parameters.name: display_currency
parameters.description:
Optional ISO-4217 currency code for the `price` fields in the response.
Defaults to the OTA's configured currency.

parameters.name: categories
parameters.description:
Optional. Limit the search to activities in these product categories.

 - UNDEFINED: Undefined category
 - RAILWAY_TICKET: Railway ticket (e.g., JR, Subway)
 - AIRPORT_TRANSPORTATION: Airport transportation (Pickup/Drop-off)
 - SHINKANSEN: Shinkansen tickets
 - EXPRESS_BUS: Highway bus tickets
 - BUS_TOUR: Bus tour (1-day or multi-day)
 - CRUISES: Cruises
 - RENTAL_CAR: Rental car
 - CHARTER: Chartered vehicle (with driver)
 - ATTRACTION: Attraction ticket
 - THEME_PARK: Theme park (e.g., Disneyland, Universal Studios)
 - MUSEUM_GALLERY: Museum or art gallery
 - AQUARIUM_ZOO: Aquarium or zoo
 - TEMPLES_SHINES: Temple or shrine visit
 - TOWER_BUILDING: Tower or landmark (e.g., Skytree, Tokyo Tower)
 - JAPANESE_RESTAURANT: Japanese restaurant
 - WESTERN_RESTAURANT: Western restaurant (e.g., steak, pasta)
 - CHINESE_RESTAURANT: Chinese restaurant
 - OTHER_RESTAURANT: Other restaurant (e.g., Korean, Indian, fusion)
 - DESSERT_BEVERAGE: Dessert or beverage (e.g., cafe, ice cream shop)
 - SIGHTSEEING_TOUR: Sightseeing tour (e.g., walking, private guide)
 - MARINE_SPORTS: Marine sports (e.g., snorkeling, diving, speedboat)
 - OUTDOOR_ACTIVITIES: Outdoor activities (e.g., hiking, skiing, rafting)
 - ONSEN: Onsen (hot spring) experience
 - SPA_MASSAGE: Spa or massage service
 - JAPANESE_CULTURAL_EXPERIENCE: Cultural experience (e.g., kimono, tea ceremony)
 - JAPANESE_CRAFT_EXPERIENCE: Traditional craft experience (e.g., dyeing, pottery)
 - JAPANESE_COOKING_EXPERIENCE: Japanese cooking experience (e.g., sushi, ramen)
 - OTHER_EXPERIENCE: Other experience
 - HOTEL: Hotel
 - RYOKAN: Ryokan (Japanese-style inn)
 - VACATION_RENTAL: Vacation rental
 - BUNDLE: Bundled product (e.g., ticket + meal)
 - PASS: Pass
 - OTHERS: Others

parameters.name: confirmation_type
parameters.description:
Optional. Limit the search to activities with the confirmation type.

 - UNDEFINED: Undefined category
 - FREE_SALE: Specific participation date, unlimited sales
 - FREE_SALE_OPEN_DATE: No specific participation date required, unlimited sales
 - INVENTORY: Specific participation date, with limited inventory
 - REQUEST: Specific participation date, manual review required for sales

get.description:
Get price and availability calendar.

This method extends the existing availability calendar by including price information. The returned calendar contains availability and corresponding prices for each date.

parameters.name: language_code
parameters.description:
Required. Display language for activity / plan / unit names in the response.
Unlike `search-activities` / `get-activity-detail` (where it is optional and omitting it returns
every language), names here are returned as plain strings in a single language, so it must be set.
Use one of the activity's `language_codes`; names may be empty for a language the activity does not provide.

parameters.name: activity_id
parameters.description: The activity identifier returned by `search-activities` or `get-activity-detail`.

parameters.name: plan_id
parameters.description: Optional plan identifier. If omitted, availability and pricing for every plan under the activity are returned.

parameters.name: target_date_from
parameters.description:
Inclusive lower bound of the calendar range, in the activity's local time zone. Format `YYYY-MM-DD`.
Must be on or before `target_date_to`.

parameters.name: target_date_to
parameters.description:
Inclusive upper bound of the calendar range, in the activity's local time zone. Format `YYYY-MM-DD`.
Must be on or after `target_date_from`.

parameters.name: display_currency
parameters.description:
Optional ISO-4217 currency code for `units[].display_amount` in the response.
Defaults to the OTA's configured currency. Does not affect `units[].payment_amount`.

post.description:
Check availability and calculate amount for a specific date.

This method retrieves availability and calculates the corresponding amount for a specific date.

Create a booking transaction. This is the first step of the booking process (Reserve phase).

Upon success, a `session_id` will be returned, which is required for the subsequent **[FinalBooking]** API call.

`participant_info` is normalized and validated before the reservation is made; see that field for the per-field rules. A request that fails validation returns HTTP 400 with one error detail per invalid field and makes no reservation.

get.description: Retrieve all pending reservation sessions for the current OTA account.

post.description:
Finalize a booking transaction. This is the second step of the booking process (Confirm phase).

Use the `session_id` obtained from **[StartBooking]** to confirm the reservation.

Cancel multiple pending reservation sessions in batch.

Provide the sessions to cancel in `booking_session_ids`. Each value is the `session_id` returned by **[StartBooking]** or listed by **[ListReservations]**. Use it to cancel unneeded reservations to avoid hitting the restriction.

get.description: Retrieve a paginated list of bookings, supporting various filters to browse records.

parameters.name: page_no
parameters.description: page number, starting from 1.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: number of bookings to return per page. Maximum 100; larger values are rejected with 400.

parameters.name: order_bys
parameters.description: Sorting criteria for the bookings. Each entry should be in the format `field_name|direction`, where `direction` is optional and can be either `asc` for ascending or `desc` for descending. If `direction` is not specified, it defaults to ascending order. Sorting criteria can only be "booking_at" for now. Default is booking_at descending.

parameters.name: booking_id
parameters.description: Filter bookings by their unique identifiers (booking_id). Multiple booking IDs can be provided to retrieve specific bookings.

parameters.name: agent_booking_id
parameters.description: Filter bookings by agent booking ids. This allows retrieval of bookings associated with specific agent reservations.

parameters.name: supplier_booking_id
parameters.description: Filter bookings by the supplier's booking identifier. This allows retrieval of bookings associated with a specific supplier booking ID.

parameters.name: booking_at_start
parameters.description: Filter bookings that were made on or after this timestamp in RFC3339 format. For timezone offsets (e.g. +09:00), URL-encode '+' as '%2B' in query strings. e.g. 2026-04-01T14:53:34.000Z

parameters.name: booking_at_end
parameters.description: Filter bookings that were made on or before this timestamp in RFC3339 format. For timezone offsets (e.g. +09:00), URL-encode '+' as '%2B' in query strings. e.g. 2026-04-01T14:53:34.000Z

parameters.name: booking_status
parameters.description:
Filter bookings by their status. Multiple statuses can be provided to retrieve bookings that match any of the specified statuses.

 - UNDEFINED: Undefined
 - REQUEST_PENDING: Such as bookingtype, REQUEST, etc supplier
 - REQUEST_REJECTED: Such as bookingtype REQUEST, supplier ( system )
 - CONFIRMED: Includesbookingtype REQUEST, supplier, bookingtype INSTANT
 - CANCELLED_BY_TRAVELER: Such as bookingtype REQUEST, PENDING | STANDBY,, PENDING, STANDBY
Cancelled BY traveler
 - CANCELLED_BY_SUPPLIER: Supplier
 - INVALID: Invalid
 - CANCEL_FAILED: Cancel failed
 - CANCEL_PENDING: ( supplier, e.g. tickethub)

post.description:
Update participant information for a confirmed booking.

Provide `booking_id` and the complete `participant_info`. The request replaces the stored participant information as a whole: any field left out is cleared, so send the full structure rather than only the changed fields (the per-participant `unit_title` is the exception: Link always fills it from the booking). Link then sends the update to the supplier and regenerates the voucher; the response carries the new voucher URLs. Sub-orders of a bulk booking cannot be updated.

The submitted `participant_info` is normalized and validated with the same rules as StartBooking (see the `participant_info` field of StartBooking for the full list) before anything is changed. Which fields are required comes from the activity's current `booking_form`. A request that fails validation returns HTTP 400 with one error detail per invalid field; the booking, the supplier and the voucher are left untouched.

Initiate a cancellation request for a confirmed booking. This is the first step of the cancellation process.

A 200 response means the booking can be cancelled and a cancellation request now exists, or an earlier open request was reused. `cancel_refund_display` holds the refund breakdown; for a bundle it is the parent's breakdown, which is the amount the OTA is charged or refunded for the whole bundle. Call **[FinalCancelBooking]** next.

`cancel_check_code` is always `CAN_BE_CANCELLED` on a 200 response. The field is deprecated and will be removed in a later version; a booking that cannot be cancelled is reported as an HTTP error with a business `error_code`, never as a 200.

Calling this endpoint again while a cancellation request is already open returns that request together with the refund amounts calculated when it was created. Those amounts are the ones FinalCancelBooking applies, so if the cancellation fee changes in between, FinalCancelBooking fails and the flow starts here again.

A 5xx or a timeout does not establish the outcome. Run StartCancelBooking → FinalCancelBooking again; resending FinalCancelBooking alone is only for a 200 with `CANCEL_PENDING` or an error with `retryable` true.

Finalize a cancellation request for a confirmed booking. This is the second step of the cancellation process.

Use the `booking_id` and specify `cancel_by` to confirm the cancellation. StartCancelBooking must have succeeded for the booking first, and the refund amounts from that response are the ones applied here.

A 200 response means the cancellation went through, or the supplier has taken it and is still confirming. Read the top-level `status`:

| status | Meaning | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CANCEL_SUCCEED` | The booking is cancelled. | Nothing. |
| `CANCEL_PENDING` | The supplier has taken the cancellation but not confirmed it yet; some suppliers handle cancellations by hand. | Call FinalCancelBooking again later to pick up the result. |

The top-level `booking_id` and `status` are the fields to read. `parent_result` is still filled for now but is deprecated and will be removed in a later version; `children_results` has been removed, and `CANCEL_FAILED` is never returned in a 200 any more.

A cancellation that did not go through is an HTTP error with a business `error_code`. For a bundle parent, one child that cannot be cancelled or whose cancellation failed makes the whole call fail with that child's error, and `metadata.booking_id` names the child. The children that were cancelled stay cancelled, and the parent's cancellation request stays open: once the cause is resolved, call FinalCancelBooking again (StartCancelBooking also works; it reuses the open request).

metadata.description:
Context for the error: request_id plus the keys documented on each error
code. Keys are never removed or renamed. The public HTTP APIs return only
these; gRPC clients and internal tools also receive further keys.

ErrorDetail.description: ErrorDetail is one entry of ErrorResponse.details.

code.description:
Canonical gRPC status code as a number (e.g. 9). The HTTP status follows
the standard google.rpc.Code mapping (9 → 400, 13 → 500, ...), except
that a request using an HTTP method the path does not accept gets HTTP
405 with code 12.

error_code.description:
Business error code, e.g. "INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE". When no business code
applies it is the canonical code name ("INTERNAL", "NOT_FOUND", ...).
Never empty. Branch on this field; treat a value you do not know as its
`code`.

message.description:
Human-readable description. Its wording may change; never parse it.
Returned as written for 4xx responses and for 5xx responses carrying a
business code; any other 5xx carries the HTTP status text only (e.g.
"Internal Server Error").

details.description:
Additional context. Each entry carries only `metadata`: request_id (quote
it when contacting support) and the keys documented for the error code.
Read error_code for the classification.

retryable.description:
Whether the SAME request may be resent as is. Always present.
  - With a business error_code: the verdict of the service that failed,
    for this response. The same code can be retryable on one endpoint
    and not on another, so this field is authoritative and the
    Transient / Terminal notes on each code are guidance.
  - With a canonical error_code: follows the code. DEADLINE_EXCEEDED,
    RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, ABORTED and UNAVAILABLE are retryable; every
    other code is not.

ErrorResponse.description:
ErrorResponse is the JSON body of every error (non-2xx) response from the
gds-neo HTTP APIs. It documents the body only; no RPC takes or returns it.
"details" entries carry no "@type" field, so parse the body with a plain
JSON decoder.

supplier_summaries.description: Suppliers contracted with this OTA. Order is not guaranteed.

id.description: Numeric internal identifier of the supplier in the GDS system.

supplier_id.description: Stable, human-readable supplier identifier used by external integrations.

original_name.description: Supplier's name in its original local language (Japanese, Chinese, etc.).

english_name.description: Supplier's English-localized name. May be empty if the supplier did not provide one.

display_price.description:
Reference "from" price of the activity, for display purposes only: the lowest `plans[].display_price`
(by gross) among the activity's plans. `gross` is the selling price and `net` is taken from the same
price entry; `net` is 0 when the caller is not allowed to see net prices.
Converted to the requested `display_currency` (OTA's configured currency when unset); always check
`currency_code` for the actual currency. Not tied to a specific date — use the availability endpoints
for the actual price of a given date.

price_exchanges.description:
Reference "from" price of the plan, for listing / display purposes only.

- Key: ISO-4217 currency code (e.g. `JPY`). The map always contains exactly one entry:
  the requested `display_currency`, or the OTA's configured currency when it is unset.
- Value: gross (selling) price for one unit of the plan's standard-price unit
  (typically the adult unit), e.g. `{"JPY": 12000}`.
- It is not tied to a specific date or plan item. Use `get-price-and-availability-calendar`
  or `check-availability-and-calculate-amount` for the actual price of a given date.

- BOOKING_CONFIRMED: relative to when the booking was confirmed
 - ACTIVITY_START: relative to the activity start time

Annual fixed date
Voucher date
Such as 07-01, representsvoucher 7/1

annual_cut_off_date.title:
Year increment reference date (MM-DD)
Voucher date,, date
Such as 04-01, represents 4/1,, 4/1

Attachment.title: Attachment information (for images, file links, etc.)

BookingField.Id.title:
- UNKNOWN: PARTICIPANT_LAST_NAME = 1; // always required
 PARTICIPANT_FIRST_NAME = 2; // always required

field_id.description:
Well-known field id, e.g. "PARTICIPANT_EMAIL_ADDRESS", "ARRIVAL_DATE",
"WEIGHT_KG". Matches the enum name from `bookingfield` package.

scope.title: where the value sits in the StartBooking payload

request_path.description:
JSON path of the value in the StartBooking payload,
e.g. "participant_info.booking_representative_fields.participant_email_address"
or "participant_info.user_information_fields[].weight_kg".

format_hint.description:
Human-readable hint of the rule StartBooking enforces on the value, e.g. "YYYY-MM-DD", "HH:mm",
"at most 100 characters", "digits, +, -, ( ) only; 8-20 characters", "ISO 3166-1 alpha-3",
"MALE, FEMALE or OTHER". Empty when nothing beyond `type` is enforced (e.g. free-text sizes).
The complete rule set, including normalization, is documented on StartBooking's `participant_info` field.

BookingForm.Type.description:
Value type of a standard booking field.

 - STRING: free-text string
 - INTEGER: integer
 - BOOLEAN: boolean
 - DATE: date "YYYY-MM-DD"
 - TIME: local time "HH:mm"
 - EMAIL: email address
 - COUNTRY_CODE: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code (see enums/countrycode)
 - LANGUAGE_CODE: language enum value (see enums/language)
 - ENUM: generic enum;

BookingType.title:
- UNDEFINED: Undefined (reserved value)
 - SINGLE: Individual
 - BULK: Bulk

description.description:
Generated description of this rule. Informational only and may be empty;
use `CancellationPolicy.custom_description` as the policy text.

applies_from.description:
The time point from which this rule takes effect.
e.g. anchor=BOOKING_CONFIRMED with no offset means the rule applies from the moment the booking is confirmed.

charge_percent.description: Percentage of the total booking amount charged (0–100).

charge_fixed.description: Fixed amount charged, in the activity's `original_currency` (not converted to `display_currency`).

CancellationRule.description: A single cancellation rule: the fee charged once applies_from has passed.

ConfirmationType.description:
- UNDEFINED: Undefined category
 - FREE_SALE: Specific participation date, unlimited sales
 - FREE_SALE_OPEN_DATE: No specific participation date required, unlimited sales
 - INVENTORY: Specific participation date, with limited inventory
 - REQUEST: Specific participation date, manual review required for sales
ConfirmationType.title: Ticket sales method

CountryCode.title:
CountryCode is defined using ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country codes.
Also includes a non-standard code UNIVERSAL for internal use.
Reference: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-3

CurrencyCode.title:
CurrencyCode is defined using ISO 4217 currency codes.
Also includes some non-standard codes used internally, such as Bitcoin (XBT), TVD, etc.
Reference: https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217

field_id.title: supplier-defined field id used as the array element key

request_path.title:
JSON path of the array element in the StartBooking payload,
e.g. "participant_info.per_booking_custom_reservation_fields[id=<field_id>].responses"

required.description:
Whether StartBooking requires this field. Derived from collecting_timing:
true when collecting_timing is ON_BOOKING, false for BEFORE_ACTIVITY and
OPTIONAL. A false here means the response is collected at some other point.
StartBooking does not ask for it, and does not reject the request without it.

title.title: i18n title shown to the traveler

description.title: i18n description shown to the traveler

choices.description:
i18n labels for CHOICE-typed fields; empty otherwise.
The value submitted in `responses` is the label string.

CustomFieldSpec.description:
Custom (supplier-defined) field descriptor. Value is submitted as
`{ id: "<field_id>", responses: [...] }` inside the corresponding
`*_custom_reservation_fields[]` array.

CustomFieldType.description:
- UNDEFINED: Undefined: reserved field
 - DATE: Date (past or future)
 - DATE_ONLY_PAST: Past date only
 - DATE_ONLY_FUTURE: Future date only
 - TIME: Time
 - YES_NO: Yes or No switch
 - DROPDOWN: Dropdown select
 - RADIO: Radio button
 - CHECK: Checkbox
 - TEXT: Single-line text input
 - TEXT_ALPHANUMERIC: Single-line text input, alphanumeric only
 - TEXT_PHONE: Single-line phone number input
 - TEXTAREA: Multi-line text input
 - TEXT_NUMERIC: Single-line text input, numeric only
CustomFieldType.title: Custom field type for ticket purchase form fields

CustomScope.description:
Whether a custom field is collected once per booking or once per participant.

 - PER_BOOKING: participant_info.per_booking_custom_reservation_fields[]
 - PER_PARTICIPANT_CUSTOM: participant_info.user_information_fields[].per_participant_custom_reservation_fields[]

num_days.title: number of days from the anchor

DayOffset.description: A day-granularity offset paired with a local time of day.

FileType.description:
- UNDEFINED: Undefined type (reserved value)
 - PDF: PDF file format (Portable Document Format)
 - IMAGE: IMAGE format (Portable Network Graphics)
 - VIDEO: VIDEO format (e.g. MP4, AVI)
 - HTML: HTML document format (HyperText Markup Language)
FileType.title: FileType represents file format types

cancellation_policy.description:
--- Legacy field, deprecated ---
Kept only for backward compatibility with existing OTA integrations.
Prefer `activity.cancellation_policy` instead. To be removed in a future major version.

supplier_id.description: supplier id. Always the same as `activity.supplier_id`.

supplier_name.description: supplier name. Always the same as `activity.supplier_name`.

min_capacity_inclusive.description: min number of booking units, e.g. 1 participant, etc.

max_capacity_inclusive.description: max number of booking units, e.g. 10 participants, etc.

meetup_or_pickup_points.title: meetup or pickup points, if any

dismissal_or_dropoff_points.title: dismissal or dropoff points, if any

booking_rule.description:
Booking rule (already resolved; apply as-is). All times are in the activity's `timezone`.
- `booking_period`: how far in advance the plan can be booked, counted from today.
- `booking_deadline`: advance-booking deadline that applies to every plan item. A date D can be booked
  until `deadline_time` on (D - `before_days`). When `booking_deadline` is absent, D can be booked until
  00:00 of D (i.e. no same-day booking).
In addition, same-day bookings are closed after `plan_items[].cutoff_time`. Both checks apply; a booking
must satisfy both. Neither applies to `FREE_SALE_OPEN_DATE` plans.

booking_form.title: booking form, describes the fields expected upon booking

display_price.description:
Reference "from" price of the plan, for display purposes only: the lowest gross price, across all of
the plan's price periods, of the plan's standard-price unit (typically the adult unit). `net` is taken
from the same price entry and is 0 when the caller is not allowed to see net prices.
Converted to the requested `display_currency` (OTA's configured currency when unset); always check
`currency_code` for the actual currency. Not tied to a specific date — use the availability endpoints
for the actual price of a given date.

title.title: plan item title (e.g. 10:00, 11:00, Full Day, etc.)

start_time.title: a HH:MM local time value indicate the start time of this plan item, if any

cutoff_time.description:
Same-day booking cutoff of the plan item, as an HH:MM local time in the activity's `timezone`, if any.
Only applies when booking for today: once this time has passed, today's slot of this plan item can no
longer be booked. Booking for a future date is governed by `booking_rule.booking_deadline` only.
Usually equal to `start_time`.

include_in_capacity.title: count as minimum booking capacity or not (e.g. baby is not counted in the booking capacity)

can_be_book_independently.title: can be booked independently or not (e.g. child cannot be booked without adult in a booking)

PeriodUnit.title:
- UNDEFINED: Undefined (reserved value)
 - DAY: Day
 - MONTH: Month
 - YEAR: Year

administrative_area_level_1.title: Google map api administrative area level 1

lat.description: Latitude in degrees. It must be in the range [-90.0, +90.0].

lon.description: Longitude in degrees. It must be in the range [-180.0, +180.0].

Scope.description:
Where the field's value lives in the StartBooking payload.

 - REPRESENTATIVE: participant_info.booking_representative_fields.<field>
 - OTHERS: participant_info.others_information_fields.<field>
 - PER_PARTICIPANT: participant_info.user_information_fields[].<field>

i18n_text.title: [(validate.rules).string = { min_len: 1 }];

duration.description:
Duration offset; negative = before the anchor, positive = after.
e.g. -259200s = 3 days before activity start.

day_offset.description:
Day-boundary offset with a specific local time (activity's `timezone`).
e.g. num_days=-3, time_of_day="23:59" = 23:59 local time, 3 calendar days before the activity date.

TimePoint.description: A point in time expressed as an offset from an anchor.

TravelProductCategory.description:
Travel product category, used for frontend categorization menus, recommendations, and analytics.
Includes categories such as transportation, dining, tickets, experiences, and accommodation.

 - UNDEFINED: Undefined category
 - RAILWAY_TICKET: Railway ticket (e.g., JR, Subway)
 - AIRPORT_TRANSPORTATION: Airport transportation (Pickup/Drop-off)
 - SHINKANSEN: Shinkansen tickets
 - EXPRESS_BUS: Highway bus tickets
 - BUS_TOUR: Bus tour (1-day or multi-day)
 - CRUISES: Cruises
 - RENTAL_CAR: Rental car
 - CHARTER: Chartered vehicle (with driver)
 - ATTRACTION: Attraction ticket
 - THEME_PARK: Theme park (e.g., Disneyland, Universal Studios)
 - MUSEUM_GALLERY: Museum or art gallery
 - AQUARIUM_ZOO: Aquarium or zoo

UnitType.description:
UnitType represents various unit types for tickets, booking items, participant categories, and other scenarios
Includes age categories, time units, pets, vehicles, people, rooms, etc.

 - AGE_ADULT_AND_CHILD: Combined adult and child type (e.g. unified pricing)
 - AGE_ADULT: Adult
 - AGE_YOUTH: Youth (e.g. middle/high school student)
 - AGE_CHILD: Child (typically ages 6-12)
 - AGE_SENIOR: Senior (e.g. age 65+)
 - AGE_INFANT: Infant (e.g. age 0-2)
 - AGE_STUDENT: Student status (unspecified level)
 - AGE_HIGH_SCHOOL: High school student
 - AGE_INTERMEDIATE_SCHOOL: Junior high school student
 - AGE_ELEMENTARY_SCHOOL: Elementary school student
 - AGE_COLLEGE: College student
 - AGE_GRADUATE: Graduate student
 - AGE_OBSERVER: Observer (non-participant)
 - AGE_ADULT_OBSERVER: Adult observer
 - AGE_CHILD_OBSERVER: Child observer
 - AGE_RIDE_ALONG: Ride-along (accompanying but not participating)
 - AGE_ADULT_RIDE_ALONG: Adult ride-along
 - AGE_CHILD_RIDE_ALONG: Child ride-along
 - AGE_DRIVER: Driver role
 - AGE_DISABLED_ADULT: Adult with disabilities
 - AGE_DISABLED_YOUTH: Youth with disabilities
 - AGE_DISABLED_CHILD: Child with disabilities
 - AGE_SUPPORTER_ADULT: Adult supporter
 - AGE_SUPPORTER_CHILD: Child supporter
 - TALL_CHILD: Tall child
 - WEIGHT_ADULT: Adult by weight (kg)
 - WEIGHT_LBS_ADULT: Adult by weight (lb)
 - MINUTES_VEHICLES: Measured in minutes (for vehicle rental)
 - HOURS_VEHICLES: Hour unit (vehicle)
 - DAYS_VEHICLES: Day unit (vehicle)
 - WEEKS_VEHICLES: Week unit (vehicle)
 - NIGHTS_VEHICLES: Night unit (vehicle)
 - MINUTES_PERSONS: Calculate personnel work time in minutes
 - HOURS_PERSONS: Calculate personnel service in hours
 - DAYS_PERSONS: Calculate personnel in days
 - WEEKS_PERSONS: Calculate personnel in weeks
 - NIGHTS_PERSONS: Calculate personnel in nights
 - MINUTE: One minute
 - HOUR: One hour
 - DAY: One day
 - WEEK: One week
 - NIGHT: One night (commonly used for lodging and activities)
 - ROOM: Number of rooms
 - QUANTITY: Custom quantity
 - CHARTER_SERVICE: Charter service
 - BOAT: Boat unit
 - GROUP: Group unit
 - PRINT: Printed/paper copy quantity
 - CHARTER_VAR: Variable charter (adjust people/hours based on situation)
 - GROUP_VAR: Variable group
 - ROOM_VAR: Variable room type
 - BOAT_VAR: Variable boat type
 - PET: General pet

 - PET_DOG: Dog (all sizes)
 - PET_DOG_S: Small dog
 - PET_DOG_M: Medium dog
 - PET_DOG_L: Large dog

VoucherExpirationPeriodType.description:
- UNDEFINED: Undefined: reserved field
 - UNLIMITED: Never expires
 - FROM_PURCHASE_DATE: Expires after a period counted from the purchase date
 - FROM_ACTIVITY_DATE: Expires after a period counted from the activity date
 - FIXED_DATE: Expires on a fixed month/day

For example: "relative fixed date = 7/1", "year increment reference date = 4/1"
This means expiry is always 7/1 each year: if purchase date is before 4/1, expiry is this year's 7/1; otherwise it is next year's 7/1

external.BookingForm.description:
BookingForm describes the fields the booking request must / may carry for a plan.

Prefer `booking_field_specs` and `custom_field_specs` (self-describing: each entry tells you the
value's JSON path in the StartBooking payload, its type, whether it is required,
and — for enum-typed fields — the allowed values). The legacy enum-id lists
under field numbers 100+ are retained for backward compatibility only and will
be removed in a future major version.

custom_description.description: Authoritative cancellation policy text written by the supplier. Show it to travelers as-is.

rules.description:
Cancellation rules, ordered most-restrictive-first.
e.g. rules[0] "not cancellable from activity start", rules[1] "100% from 24h before", rules[2] "free from booking confirmation".
To estimate the fee for a given cancellation time, take the first rule whose `applies_from` is not after that time.

external.CancellationPolicy.description:
CancellationPolicy describes the cancellation fees of an activity.

- `custom_description` is the authoritative policy text. Show it to travelers as-is.
- `rules` is a structured form of the same policy, for display or estimation only.
  `rules[].description` is informational, may be empty, and must not be used in place of `custom_description`.
- The fee actually charged is always determined server-side at cancel time; `StartCancelBooking` returns it.

year.description:
Year of date. Must be from 1 to 9999, or 0 if specifying a date without
a year.

month.description: Month of year. Must be from 1 to 12.

day.description:
Day of month. Must be from 1 to 31 and valid for the year and month, or 0
if specifying a year/month where the day is not significant.

neo_datetime.Date.description:
Represents a whole calendar date, e.g. date of birth. The time of day and
time zone are either specified elsewhere or are not significant. The date
is relative to the Proleptic Gregorian Calendar. The day may be 0 to
represent a year and month where the day is not significant, e.g. credit card
expiration date. The year may be 0 to represent a month and day independent
of year, e.g. anniversary date.

AllotmentType.title:
- PLAN_ITEM_SHARED: Shared across plan items, e.g. 10:00 and 14:00 map to the same inventory
 - UNIT_SHARED: Shared across units, e.g. adult and child map to the same inventory
 - PLAN_ITEM_AND_UNIT_SHARED: Shared across both plan item and unit
 - INDEPENDENT: Independent inventory

language_code.description:
Required. Display language for activity / plan names in the response.
Unlike `search-activities` / `get-activity-detail` (where it is optional and omitting it returns
every language), names here are returned as plain strings in a single language, so it must be set.
Use one of the activity's `language_codes`; names may be empty for a language the activity does not provide.

activity_id.description: The activity identifier returned by `search-activities` or `get-activity-detail`.

plan_id.description: The plan identifier. Returns `NOT_FOUND` if the plan does not belong to the activity.

plan_item_id.description:
The plan item identifier, from `plans[].plan_items[].plan_item_id` of `get-activity-detail`.
If it does not belong to the plan, the response is returned with `availability_status` = `NG` and zero amounts.

target_date.description:
The date to check, in the activity's local time zone. Format `YYYY-MM-DD`.
Returns `FAILED_PRECONDITION` if the date has passed or the plan item's same-day cutoff time has passed.

units.description:
The units and quantities to check.
Each `plan_unit_id` should appear at most once.

display_currency.description:
Optional ISO-4217 currency code for `plan_items[].display_amount` in the response.
Defaults to the OTA's configured currency. Does not affect `original_amount` or `payment_amount`.

activity_id.description: The activity identifier, same as the request.

plan_id.description: The plan identifier, same as the request.

target_date.description: The checked date, same as the request. Format `YYYY-MM-DD`.

plan_items.description: Always contains exactly one entry: the requested plan item.

language_code.description: The language used for names in this response, same as the request.

plan_item_id.description: The plan item identifier. Empty if `plan_item_id` in the request does not belong to the plan.

confirmation_type.description: How bookings for this plan are confirmed.

original_amount.description:
Total amount in the supplier's currency: the sum of each unit's price × `request_quantity`.
This is the price before currency conversion, not a price before discount.
All three amounts are `0` when `availability_status` is `NG`.
In all three amounts, `net` is 0 when the caller is not allowed to see net prices.

display_amount.description: Same total as `original_amount`, converted to `display_currency` at the current exchange rate.

payment_amount.description:
Same total as `original_amount`, converted to the OTA's configured settlement currency.
This is the amount used for billing, regardless of `display_currency`.

activity_id.description: The activity identifier, same as the request.

plans.description: One entry per plan. Contains only the requested plan when `plan_id` is set.

language_code.description: The language used for names in this response, same as the request.

date.description: Date in the activity's local time zone. Format `YYYY-MM-DD`.

plan_items.description:
Plan items (time slots / sessions) for this date, sorted by `plan_item_name`.
Empty when the plan has no inventory set up for this date.

confirmation_type.description: How bookings for this plan are confirmed.

days.description: One entry per date from `target_date_from` to `target_date_to`, both inclusive, in ascending order.

units.description:
Units (ticket types such as adult / child) that have a price on this date.
Empty when no price is set for this date; such a date cannot be booked.

start_time.description:
Start time of this plan item in the activity's local time zone. Format `HH:MM`. Empty if the plan item
has no fixed start time.

allotment_quantity.description:
Remaining inventory of the plan item on this date. This is a single pool shared by all units of the
plan item (see `allotment_type`), so every unit under the same plan item has the same value.
`0` when sold out, when the booking window has closed, or when the same-day cutoff time has passed.

availability_status.description:
`OK` when `allotment_quantity` is greater than 0, otherwise `NG`.
This is a quick indicator for display only. Call `check-availability-and-calculate-amount` to confirm
availability for a specific quantity before booking.

display_amount.description:
Price of ONE unit (not multiplied by any quantity), in `display_currency`.
`gross` is the selling price; `net` is the OTA's purchase price, and is 0 when the caller is not allowed to see net prices.
Converted from the supplier's currency at the current exchange rate when the currencies differ.

payment_amount.description:
Price of ONE unit (not multiplied by any quantity), in the OTA's configured settlement currency.
This is the amount used for billing, regardless of `display_currency`.

unit_type.description: The unit category, e.g. adult or child.

plan_unit_id.description:
The unit identifier, from `plans[].units[].plan_unit_id` of `get-activity-detail`.
Unknown identifiers are ignored and do not count toward the amount or the quantity check.

request_quantity.description: Number of this unit to book.

Link does not check the format and sets no length limit, but keep it short. It is stored on the cancellation record for audit and returned as `cancel_by` in the `CANCELED` webhook.

parent_result.description: Deprecated; read the top-level `booking_id` and `status` instead. Still filled for now (same booking and status as the top-level fields); will be removed in a later version.

booking_id.description: The booking the request was made for (the bundle parent for a bundle). Present on every 200 response.

status.description: Outcome of this call. `CANCEL_SUCCEED`: the booking is cancelled. `CANCEL_PENDING`: the supplier has taken the cancellation but not confirmed it yet; call FinalCancelBooking again later. A cancellation that did not go through is an HTTP error, so `CANCEL_FAILED` never appears here.

QRCodeCodeType.description:
- UNDEFINED: Reserved field, undefined category
 - QRCODE: QR code (Quick Response Code): 2D barcode that can store large amounts of text or URL data
 - TEXT: Plain text (e.g. redemption code, serial number) displayed directly without generating a barcode
 - HYPERLINK: URL format, rendered directly as a hyperlink (e.g. redemption page)
 - BARCODE128: Code 128 barcode: highly versatile, supports digits and letters, commonly used in logistics and ticketing
 - BARCODE93: Code 93 barcode: more compact than Code 39, can encode more data, common in aviation and logistics
 - BARCODE39: Code 39 barcode: supports uppercase letters and digits only, commonly used for IDs and simple applications
 - BARCODE25: Code 25 barcode (Interleaved 2 of 5): supports digits only, common in inventory and industrial manufacturing
 - SUPPLIER_QRCODE_URL: For some suppliers, the booking adapter retrieves a supplier-provided QR code URL, stores it in our own GCS, then serves it to frontend clients
QRCodeCodeType.title: QRCodeCodeType represents the code types shown on vouchers for identifying and displaying different barcode or data formats

 - FIXED: Fixed-amount refund
 - PERCENTAGE: Fixed-percentage refund
 - NOT_CANCELLATION: Non-refundable
 - NOT_YET_CHARGED: Not paid yet, so no refund is processed
 - FULL_REFUND: Full refund
 - REFUND_FAILED: Refund failed (reason is written in refund_failed_reason)

booking_id.description: The unique identifier of the booking.

status.description: Deprecated together with `parent_result`; read the top-level `status` instead. On a 200 response this is `CANCEL_SUCCEED` or `CANCEL_PENDING`; `CANCEL_FAILED` is never returned any more.

failed_reason.example: Cancellation failed due to supplier restrictions.
failed_reason.description: Deprecated. Always null: a failed cancellation is an HTTP error whose `message` carries the reason.

language_code.description: Language used for response content and voucher language. This is an enum field; please provide the string representation of the enum value. Must be one of the languages configured on the target Activity (`activity.langs`); otherwise the request is rejected with `InvalidArgument` and `errdetails.ErrorInfo` carrying `LANGUAGE_CODE`, `ALLOWED_LANGS`, and `ACTIVITY_ID`.

country_code.description: Country code of the OTA placing the booking, in ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 format. This is an enum field; please provide the string representation of the enum value, for example "JPN". Fill in your own country; the same fixed value can be sent on every request. Optional: when it is omitted, the booking records `UNIVERSAL`. Link keeps it on the booking for its own finance records; it is not sent to the supplier and does not affect the price. It is not the participant's country: that is `participant_info.booking_representative_fields.participant_resident_region`, the country the participant lives in, which is sent to suppliers that need it, printed on the voucher, and required or optional depending on the activity's booking form. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-3

target_date.description: Required for StartBooking unless the booking rule's confirmation_type is 'FREE_SALE_OPEN_DATE'. Date of the activity in YYYY-MM-DD format, interpreted in the activity's timezone.

plan_unit_items.description: Participant types, and their quantity (eg. Adults x 2, Children x 3)

display_currency_code.description: ISO 4217 currency code used for `display_currency_price` in the response. LINK converts the Supplier's currency into this currency for prices displayed to the traveler. If no converted price needs to be displayed, specify a fixed currency, such as Japanese yen, and disregard the corresponding `display_currency_price` returned in the response.

participant_info.description:
Participant information.

At least one of `first_name` / `last_name` (the booking representative) must be non-empty. Which other fields are required comes from the activity's `booking_form` (GetActivityDetail); the rules below apply to every field that is sent, required or not. An optional string that is empty or only whitespace counts as not sent. Violations are rejected with HTTP 400 and one `ErrorInfo` detail per field (`field` = JSON path of the value, `constraint` = the rule it broke).

**Normalization (applied before validation; the normalized value is what gets stored, printed on the voucher and sent to the supplier)**
- Leading and trailing whitespace is removed from every string in `booking_representative_fields` and `others_information_fields`, and from `passport_number`, `date_of_birth`, `gender`, `eyesight`, `weight_kg`, `height_cm`, `shoe_size_cm` and `clothes_size` of each participant. `passport_first_name` / `passport_last_name` are not trimmed.
- `hotel_tel`, `destination_tel`: all whitespace removed.
- `arrival_flight_number`, `departure_flight_number`: whitespace and hyphens removed, then upper-cased (`nh-842` -> `NH842`).
- `gender`, `passport_number`: upper-cased. `passport_first_name`, `passport_last_name`: curly quotes, dashes and full-width spaces are folded to their ASCII forms, then upper-cased.

**booking_representative_fields**
- `participant_email_address`, `destination_email`: valid email address, at most 254 characters.
- `hotel_name`: at most 100 characters. `hotel_address`: at most 200 characters.
- `hotel_reservation_last_name`, `hotel_reservation_first_name`: letters of any language, spaces, `'`, `-` and `.` only; at most 50 characters.
- `hotel_tel`, `destination_tel`: digits, `+`, `-`, `(` and `)` only; 8 to 20 characters after whitespace removal.
- `arrival_date`, `departure_date`: `YYYY-MM-DD`; `arrival_date` must not be after `departure_date`.
- `arrival_time`, `departure_time`: `HH:mm`, 24-hour, hours and minutes only (`09:30` or `9:30`; no seconds, no trailing text).
- `arrival_flight_number`, `departure_flight_number`: after normalization, 3 to 8 letters or digits containing at least one letter and one digit, e.g. `NH842`, `5J123`, `ANA842`.
- `participant_resident_region`: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code. `participant_language`: a supported language enum value. `UNDEFINED` is rejected for both.

**others_information_fields**
- `passengers_quantity`, `participants_quantity`, `luggage_quantity`, `children_without_seat_quantity`, `child_seat_quantity_paid`, `child_seat_quantity_free`: integer, 0 or more.
- `preferred_start_time`: `HH:mm`, same rule as `arrival_time`.
- `preferred_pick_up_location`, `preferred_drop_off_location`: at most 200 characters.
- `preferred_guide_language_code`, `preferred_driver_language_code`: a supported language enum value.

**user_information_fields[]**
- `passport_first_name`, `passport_last_name`: English letters, spaces, `'`, `-` and `.` only, as printed in the passport's machine-readable zone; at most 50 characters each (surrounding spaces count).
- `passport_nationality`: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code; `UNDEFINED` is rejected.
- `passport_number`: letters and digits only, 6 to 12 characters.
- `date_of_birth`: `YYYY-MM-DD`; no range check.
- `age`: 0 to 120; not cross-checked against `date_of_birth`.
- `gender`: `MALE`, `FEMALE` or `OTHER` (accepted in any letter case, stored upper-cased).
- `diving_experience_times`: 0 to 9999.
- `eyesight`, `weight_kg`, `height_cm`, `shoe_size_cm`, `clothes_size`: free text, no format rule.

agent_booking_id.description: Agent Booking ID. This is a custom booking reference ID provided by the agent. It can be used to link the booking in GDS with the agent's internal system.

agent_reservation_note.description: Agent Reservation Note. This is a custom note provided by the agent for the reservation. It can be used to store any additional information related to the booking that the agent wants to keep track of.

idempotent_key.description:
idempotent_key is an optional key from the caller. It makes retrying StartBooking safe: a retry with the same key will not create a second reservation. Keys longer than 64 bytes are invalid.

The first call's reservation stays open until booking_session_expire_at. Send the same key again in that window and StartBooking returns the same reservation, with the same session_id, prices and expiry. A retry counts as the same reservation only when the activity, plan, plan item, units, target date and display currency all match; if any of them differ, the call fails rather than starting a second reservation. participant_info, language, country and notes are not part of that check, so a retry that changes them still books the values from the first call. While an earlier StartBooking or FinalBooking for the key is still running, the call fails as in use and can be retried a few seconds later.

After the reservation expires with no FinalBooking, the key is free again and the next call starts a new reservation. After a booking is placed with the key, or an earlier attempt is left in a state that needs manual handling, the key can never book again, and that block does not expire. Send a new idempotent_key to start a fresh attempt in those cases, or whenever an attempt looks stuck.

Note that session_id is derived from the key, so the same key always yields the same session_id, even for a new reservation. A matching session_id alone does not mean the response was a replay.

session_id.description: The booking session ID. Use this in the subsequent **[FinalBooking]** or **[CancelReservations]** API call.

booking_id.description: Booking reference ID. Normally identical to the `booking_id` returned by the subsequent **[FinalBooking]** call, so it can already be recorded at the reserve phase.

supplier_currency_price.description: Price details in the supplier's currency.

payment_currency_price.description: Price details in the payment's currency.

display_currency_price.description: Price details in the display's currency.

expiry.description: Session expiry time in RFC 3339 format. Normally non-null. If the booking adapter does not provide an expiry, a 15-minute fallback is applied.

booking_rule.description: Booking rule details, including participant info requirements.

unit_prices.description:
One entry per unit requested in `plan_unit_items`, identified by `plan_unit_id`. The three prices are for a single unit; multiply by `count` for the unit's subtotal.

When tickets are sold between a Supplier and an OTA, different currencies may be used by each party, as illustrated below:

  - Supplier currency: Japanese yen  
    Example: Tokyo Metro
  - OTA payment currency: U.S. dollars  
    Example: An OTA that settles with LINK in U.S. dollars
  - Currency displayed to the traveler: Chinese yuan  
    Example: A traveler from China purchasing a ticket for Japan through that OTA

In this case, each price field is used as follows:

  - `supplier_currency_price`  
    The original price of the product in the currency provided by the Supplier. In the example above, this is the price in Japanese yen.

  - `payment_currency_price`  
    The price converted by LINK from the Supplier's currency into the OTA's payment currency. In the example above, this is the price converted from Japanese yen to U.S. dollars.

  - `display_currency_price`  
    The price converted by LINK from the Supplier's currency into the currency displayed to the traveler. In the example above, this is the price converted from Japanese yen to Chinese yuan.

Please note that the currency used by `display_currency_price` is determined by the `display_currency_code` specified in the request payload.

If there is no need to display a converted price to the traveler, you may specify a fixed currency, such as Japanese yen, in `display_currency_code` and simply disregard the corresponding `display_currency_price` returned in the response.

cancel_check_code.description: Deprecated. Always `CAN_BE_CANCELLED` on a 200 response: a booking that cannot be cancelled is reported as an HTTP error with a business `error_code`. The field will be removed in a later version; do not branch on it.

cancel_refund_display.description:
Refund display information for the cancellation. When tickets are sold between a Supplier and an OTA, different currencies may be used by each party, as illustrated below:

  - Supplier currency: Japanese yen  
    Example: Tokyo Metro
  - OTA payment currency: U.S. dollars  
    Example: An OTA that settles with LINK in U.S. dollars
  - Currency displayed to the traveler: Chinese yuan  
    Example: A traveler from China purchasing a ticket for Japan through that OTA

In this case, each price field is used as follows:

  - `supplier_currency_price`  
    The original price of the product in the currency provided by the Supplier. In the example above, this is the price in Japanese yen.

  - `payment_currency_price`  
    The price converted by LINK from the Supplier's currency into the OTA's payment currency. In the example above, this is the price converted from Japanese yen to U.S. dollars.

  - `display_currency_price`  
    The price converted by LINK from the Supplier's currency into the currency displayed to the traveler. In the example above, this is the price converted from Japanese yen to Chinese yuan.

Please note that the currency used by `display_currency_price` is determined by the `display_currency_code` specified in the original StartBooking request payload.

If there is no need to display a converted price to the traveler, you may specify a fixed currency, such as Japanese yen, in `display_currency_code` when starting the booking and simply disregard the corresponding `display_currency_price` returned in the response.

participant_info.description:
Updated participant information for the booking. This will completely overwrite the existing participant information.

The same normalization and validation rules as `participant_info` in StartBooking apply (see that field for the full per-field list); the activity's current `booking_form` decides which fields are required. If validation fails the call returns HTTP 400 with one `ErrorInfo` detail per field and nothing is changed: the stored participant information, the supplier booking and the voucher all stay as they were.

voucher_urls.description: Updated voucher URLs after participant info modification.

plan_unit_id.description: Plan Unit ID that this participant belongs to (e.g. adult, child). Get this value from [get-activity-detail] API response.

supplier_ticket_id.title: Supplier ticket ID, assigned by backend booking adapter and displayed on voucher (not submitted by frontend)

has_any_field.title: Whether any optional field is set

passport_first_name.title: Participant first name (romanized as on passport)

passport_last_name.title: Participant last name (romanized as on passport)

gender.description: Gender, value has to be "MALE", "FEMALE" or "OTHER". Accepted case-insensitively; stored and returned upper-cased.

booking_id.description: The unique identifier of the booking.

supplier_booking_id.description: The unique identifier of the booking in the supplier's system.

agent_booking_id.description: The unique identifier of the booking in the agent's system.

agent_reservation_note.description: The note of the booking in the agent's system.

status.description: The current status of the booking. `CANCEL_FAILED` can still appear here even though FinalCancelBooking never returns it: Link sets it when a FinalCancelBooking failed after the supplier had already accepted the cancellation (that call returned an HTTP error), or when a bundle parent's cancellation stopped because a child booking failed or is still waiting for its supplier. Such a booking is not cancelled. A bundle parent can be resumed by calling FinalCancelBooking again; otherwise call StartCancelBooking again to retry, and contact support if it fails again.

plan_item_id.description: The unique identifier of the plan item.

plan_title_traveler_language.description: The title of the plan in the traveler's language.

target_date.description: Date of the activity in the timezone defined by the activity's `timezone` field.

expiration_date.description: Voucher expiration date and time, based on the activity's timezone.

booking_at.description: Booking that was made on this timestamp in RFC3339 format. e.g. 2026-04-01T14:53:34.000Z

booking_date.description: Date when the booking was made, based on the activity's timezone.

issued_status.description: The voucher issuance status for the booking.

issued_status_updated_at.description: Timestamp in RFC3339 format of the booking's redemption. For a single booking it is set when issued_status first becomes ISSUED or PARTIAL, moves forward when PARTIAL becomes ISSUED, and stays unchanged when ISSUED becomes PARTIAL (some tickets were reverted) or when issued_status does not change. For a bundle parent it always equals the latest issued_status_updated_at among its redeemed child bookings, so it is refreshed whenever that value changes and can move backwards when the most recently redeemed child is reverted. null when the booking is not issued, including after an issuance is reverted. e.g. 2026-04-01T14:53:34.000Z

order_count.description: The total quantity of units ordered for the booking.

participant_resident_region.description: Country the participant lives in, in ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 format, as sent in `participant_info.booking_representative_fields.participant_resident_region`. Not the same as the `country_code` sent in StartBooking, which is the OTA's own country.

destination_email.description: Destination email address for booking-related notifications.

refund_rule_type.description: The kind of cancellation fee rule that produced the amounts. `FIXED`: a fixed fee. `PERCENTAGE`: a percentage of the price. `FULL_REFUND`: no fee. `NOT_YET_CHARGED`: a REQUEST booking cancelled before it was charged, so there is nothing to refund. `NOT_CANCELLATION` is no longer produced: a booking whose policy forbids cancellation is rejected by StartCancelBooking with `BOOKING_NOT_CANCELLABLE`, so it only appears in GetBooking for bookings cancelled before that check existed. `REFUND_FAILED` appears only when the booking's cancellation policy has no fee rule Link can apply; the amounts then show no fee and `refund_failed_reason` says why. Contact support in that case.

refund_failed_reason.example: Refund not applicable due to non-refundable policy.
refund_failed_reason.description: Set only when `refund_rule_type` is `REFUND_FAILED`: a short English note for support explaining why the cancellation policy could not be applied. Its wording may change; do not parse it.

cancel_at.description: The time of cancellation in RFC3339 format.
